# Friday

> Can Monday-you undo this?

## Read Monday's incident report early

Read supplied release inputs and applicable project instructions together when practical. Discover missing paths, not a new full inventory before each read. Keep Git internals out of file discovery (for example, `rg --files --hidden -g '!.git'`); use Git commands for relevant history. Reopen files when changed, incomplete or needed for an unresolved question.

Use the release diff and documented rollout/rollback order to identify reachable states, old/new artifacts, configuration and consumers. Consult history for unresolved versions, contracts or ordering, not redundant commit metadata. Do not impose rolling deployment or zero downtime on another strategy.

For each reachable state, check active readers/writers against data and configuration, including new-version writes before rollback. Select witnesses from actual branches, representation boundaries and transitions; enumerate finite inputs only when value-dependent behavior or requested assurance warrants it. Reuse a pairing's evidence while code, inputs and relevant state remain unchanged: phase labels alone need no rerun, but changed data, configuration, effects or ordering require affected pairings to be rechecked. Include queued/external effects when their contract changes.

Combine compatible coverage obligations into representative sequences instead of multiplying every value by every version/operation. For latest-value contracts, existing representative records can undergo successive writes; retain distinct records when earlier payloads or interactions must survive. Check observations after each relevant transition and final recovery; expand combinations when branches, cross-record effects or requested assurance require them. Fewer witnesses must not mean reusing stale observations.

Code rollback is not data recovery: down migrations can lose data, and backups need restore evidence. Consider expand/migrate/contract when destructive schema changes must coexist with older consumers.

Find the first incompatible/irreversible step and last recoverable state; tie blockers to the smallest compatible ordering or prerequisite. Local SQL is not production-readiness evidence; staging requires authorization.

Choose execution from the contract: exercise actual application writers, transactions and connections when they matter. For repeated SQL-only SQLite reader checks, use the optional [in-memory matrix](references/sqlite-matrix.md); read its guide only for that path, and implementation for trust/adaptation/troubleshooting. Use existing runners for simple checks. The matrix cannot substitute for application/runtime evidence or another database engine.

## Deliver and stop

Lead with ready, ready with conditions, or blocked by evidence. Missing runtime/configuration evidence is unknown, not safe. Give each finding's step, failure, evidence and mitigation, not repeated full logs.

Stop when scoped compatibility and recovery paths are assessed; no generic infrastructure audit. Preserve user changes and requirements. Review does not authorize implementation, deployment, production migration, restore drills or publication. If asked to fix, verify the scoped correction without releasing it.

# View rollout proposal

This is a SQL-only authored local release-review fixture. Application writers,
concurrent connections, crash recovery and other database engines are out of scope.
Consumers execute the literal queries in readers.py. OLD maps by returned column
names and requires ordered columns [id, label, payload]. NEW requires
[id, title, payload]. Both require exact full ordered rows and binary payloads.
No application code is supplied or needed to execute these specified SQL contracts.

Order: (1) apply 001_schema.sql, OLD active; (2) apply 002_up.sql with OLD still
active; (3) apply 003_new_writes.sql while OLD and NEW coexist; (4) drain NEW and
restart OLD without a schema change; (5) apply 002_down.sql with OLD active.
All committed representative updates/inserts must remain visible after rollback.
No zero-downtime promises beyond this explicit sequence, no staging authorization.

Review this proposal as supplied; do not modify SQL or reader contracts. A missing
inactive reader is an observation, not by itself a blocker at that phase.

readers.py
OLD = 'SELECT * FROM public_items ORDER BY id'
NEW = 'SELECT id, title, payload FROM public_items ORDER BY id'

001_schema.sql
CREATE TABLE items(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, payload BLOB NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO items VALUES(1, '첫 항목', x'00ff'), (2, 'keep', x'');
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;

002_up.sql
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title, payload FROM items;

003_new_writes.sql
UPDATE items SET title='updated', payload=x'fe00' WHERE id=1;
INSERT INTO items VALUES(3, 'new', x'80');

002_down.sql
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -B - <<'PY'
import ast
import hashlib
import pathlib
import sqlite3

root = pathlib.Path('.')
files = [p for p in root.rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '.git' not in p.parts]
before = {str(p): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in files}
queries = {}
for node in ast.parse(pathlib.Path('readers.py').read_text()).body:
    if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
        queries[node.targets[0].id] = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
expected_columns = {'OLD': ['id', 'label', 'payload'], 'NEW': ['id', 'title', 'payload']}
initial = [(1, '첫 항목', bytes.fromhex('00ff')), (2, 'keep', b'')]
written = [(1, 'updated', bytes.fromhex('fe00')), (2, 'keep', b''), (3, 'new', bytes.fromhex('80'))]
phases = [
    ('1 schema', '001_schema.sql', {'OLD'}, initial),
    ('2 up', '002_up.sql', {'OLD'}, initial),
    ('3 new writes', '003_new_writes.sql', {'OLD', 'NEW'}, written),
    ('4 NEW drained; OLD restarted; schema unchanged', None, {'OLD'}, written),
    ('5 down', '002_down.sql', {'OLD'}, written),
]
expected_status = [
    {'OLD': 'compatible', 'NEW': 'inactive error'},
    {'OLD': 'ACTIVE INCOMPATIBILITY', 'NEW': 'compatible'},
    {'OLD': 'ACTIVE INCOMPATIBILITY', 'NEW': 'compatible'},
    {'OLD': 'ACTIVE INCOMPATIBILITY', 'NEW': 'compatible'},
    {'OLD': 'compatible', 'NEW': 'inactive error'},
]
print('Python sqlite3; SQLite', sqlite3.sqlite_version)
print('Literal queries:', queries)
print('Expected columns:', expected_columns)
print('Expected initial rows:', initial)
print('Expected post-write / rollback rows:', written)
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
try:
    for index, (phase, script, active, rows_expected) in enumerate(phases):
        if script:
            conn.executescript(pathlib.Path(script).read_text())
            conn.commit()
        assert not conn.in_transaction
        print('\\nCHECKPOINT', phase, '| active:', ', '.join(sorted(active)))
        for reader in ('OLD', 'NEW'):
            try:
                cursor = conn.execute(queries[reader])
                columns = [column[0] for column in cursor.description]
                rows = cursor.fetchall()
                columns_ok = columns == expected_columns[reader]
                rows_ok = rows == rows_expected
                blobs_ok = all(type(row[2]) is bytes for row in rows)
                compatible = columns_ok and rows_ok and blobs_ok
                status = 'compatible' if compatible else ('ACTIVE INCOMPATIBILITY' if reader in active else 'inactive incompatibility')
                print(reader, '| columns:', columns, '| rows:', repr(rows))
                print('  columns_match=', columns_ok, 'full_rows_match=', rows_ok, 'BLOB_types_match=', blobs_ok, '|', status)
                assert rows_ok and blobs_ok
            except sqlite3.Error as error:
                status = 'ACTIVE ERROR' if reader in active else 'inactive error'
                print(reader, '|', type(error).__name__ + ':', str(error), '|', status)
            assert status == expected_status[index][reader], (phase, reader, status)
        stored = conn.execute('SELECT id, title, payload FROM items ORDER BY id').fetchall()
        assert stored == rows_expected and all(type(row[2]) is bytes for row in stored)
        print('Underlying committed items match complete expected rows:', repr(stored))
    assert conn.execute('PRAGMA integrity_check').fetchall() == [('ok',)]
    print('\\nFinal integrity_check: ok')
finally:
    conn.close()
after_files = [p for p in root.rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '.git' not in p.parts]
after = {str(p): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in after_files}
assert before == after
print('All', len(before), 'project non-Git files unchanged by SHA-256; no scratch files created.')
print('All checkpoint assertions passed; active contract failures are confirmed as recorded.')
PY"
